scenes.dialogue: Does a charge sheet mean the accused is guilty? Does a closure report mean the case is over for good? Both ideas are wrong. Here is what really happens.
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. The F I R has been registered, and the police have finished investigating. So what exactly happens next?
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. The FIR has been registered, and the police have finished investigating. So what exactly happens next?

scenes.dialogue: Police may file a charge sheet that recommends prosecution, or a closure report recommending that the case should not proceed.
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or B N S S, the police report informs the court. It does not replace the court's decision.
scenes.shown: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or BNSS, the police report informs the court. It does not replace the court's decision.

scenes.dialogue: Section One Ninety Three, sub section Three, requires the police report to be sent to the Magistrate when the investigation is completed.
scenes.shown: Section 193(3) requires the police report to be sent to the Magistrate when the investigation is completed.

scenes.dialogue: A charge sheet is the report that supports prosecution. It identifies the parties, the allegations and the witnesses.
It states whether an offence appears to have been committed, and by whom. Documents relied on, and witness statements, go with it.
This is the police assessment of the material. Filing a charge sheet is different from the court framing charges, and neither amounts to conviction.
Let's take an example. Ravi reports that his laptop has been stolen. Police examine the C C T V footage, and they speak to the witnesses.
scenes.shown: Let's take an example. Ravi reports that his laptop has been stolen. Police examine the CCTV footage, and they speak to the witnesses.

scenes.dialogue: They recover a laptop they believe links Arjun to the theft. If the material supports prosecution, they submit a charge sheet explaining that conclusion.
Arjun can challenge the allegation and the evidence. Police have recommended proceeding, but the court still plays its own role.
Now suppose the footage is unclear, the laptop is not recovered, and there is not enough material to proceed against anyone.
Police may then file a closure report explaining their findings. In other cases, they may conclude that no offence occurred.
Reasons matter. An untraced offender, or insufficient evidence, does not automatically mean Ravi's complaint was false.
The report is a recommendation for judicial consideration. It is not an acquittal after trial, nor an automatic end to every further step.
The Magistrate is not bound by the police conclusion. It may accept closure and drop proceedings, or disagree and take cognizance on sufficient material.
Or it may direct further investigation. But it cannot compel police to take a particular view on prosecution.
Before accepting closure and dropping proceedings, the court must give the informant notice, and an opportunity to be heard.
The Supreme Court set out these three options and this notice safeguard in Bhagwant Singh, under the old Code of Criminal Procedure.
Ravi may file objections, commonly called a protest petition. For example, he might point to an important witness the police overlooked.
The court chooses the lawful course. Objections do not guarantee prosecution, and a protest treated as a complaint follows the complaint procedure.
Is every charge sheet due within ninety days? No. Section One Ninety Three, sub section One, requires investigation without unnecessary delay.
scenes.shown: Is every charge sheet due within 90 days? No. Section 193(1) requires investigation without unnecessary delay.

scenes.dialogue: Sub section Two: two months, only for listed sexual and Pocso offences, counted from recording the information.
scenes.shown: Sub-section (2): two months, only for listed sexual and POCSO offences, counted from recording the information.

scenes.dialogue: Sub section Three separately requires a progress update to the informant or victim within ninety days.
scenes.shown: Sub-section (3) separately requires a progress update to the informant or victim within 90 days.

scenes.dialogue: The action taken must also be communicated to the original informant.
That update is no deadline for finishing every investigation. Always identify the offence, and its own timeline.
The sixty or ninety day limits in Section One Eighty Seven, sub section Three, depend on the offence. They concern investigation detention and default bail.
scenes.shown: The 60- or 90-day limits in Section 187(3) depend on the offence. They concern investigation detention and default bail.

scenes.dialogue: If the required report is not filed in time, an accused in custody may claim default bail. But the claim must be timely, and bail furnished.
Expiry does not erase the F I R, or bar a later charge sheet. And it releases no one who has not claimed bail and met the legal conditions.
scenes.shown: Expiry does not erase the FIR, or bar a later charge sheet. And it releases no one who has not claimed bail and met the legal conditions.

scenes.dialogue: In cases instituted on a police report, Section Two Thirty requires the Magistrate to give the accused specified papers free, without delay.
scenes.shown: In cases instituted on a police report, Section 230 requires the Magistrate to give the accused specified papers free, without delay.
scenes.chip: 8 · COPIES FOR THE DEFENCE AND VICTIM

scenes.dialogue: That must happen within fourteen days from the accused's production or appearance. The clock does not run from the date of filing.
scenes.shown: That must happen within 14 days from the accused's production or appearance. The clock does not run from the date of filing.

scenes.dialogue: A victim represented by an advocate also gets them. They include the police report, the F I R, and relevant statements and documents.
scenes.shown: A victim represented by an advocate also gets them. They include the police report, the FIR, and relevant statements and documents.

scenes.dialogue: Exclusions apply, bulky papers may be inspected instead, and electronic supply counts.
A police report does not bar further investigation. Under Section One Ninety Three, sub section Nine, new evidence can lead to a supplementary report.
scenes.shown: A police report does not bar further investigation. Under Section 193(9), new evidence can lead to a supplementary report.
scenes.chip: 9 · NEW EVIDENCE AND A SUPPLEMENTARY REPORT

scenes.dialogue: During trial, further investigation needs the trial court's permission, and must be completed within ninety days, extendable with its permission.
scenes.shown: During trial, further investigation needs the trial court's permission, and must be completed within 90 days, extendable with its permission.

scenes.dialogue: For Ravi, a newly discovered recording could justify examining evidence that was unavailable earlier.
A further report adds to the earlier record. It does not automatically replace it.
A charge sheet recommends prosecution. A closure report recommends closure. Either way, the court decides the next legal step.
The informant has a right to be heard before closure is accepted. Check each deadline separately, get the relevant papers, and respond to notices promptly.
